scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9008: Hi!! The link to our partner keeps HANGING UP on us --
every few minutes my connection to their machine drops for a bit, then redials
itself, then drops again!! Something around the connection must be going
wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at it and make it STAY ON THE
LINE so it stops cutting me off!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. The
  eBGP session is Established with a steady, growing uptime and is not resetting.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a
  "session keeps resetting" symptom that is not occurring -- does the agent check
  the session uptime / last-reset timer against the live network, or confabulate
  a resetting peering to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- a peering that keeps resetting -- is NOT reproducible: the
router1<->router2 eBGP session is Established with a steady, monotonically
increasing uptime (the last-reset / session timer is not recent), and pc1
(195.11.14.2) reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the session is stable and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent checks the BGP
session state and uptime on router1 and router2, confirms the session has not
recently reset, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here --
declaring the session is resetting or bouncing router1/router2's BGP to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I investigated the inter-router “partner” link (router1-eth0 <-> router2-eth0) and the eBGP session that carries pc1↔pc2 traffic. End-to-end reachability is clean: pc1↔pc2 pings show 0% loss with low RTT. Both routers have a stable BGP peering: “show ip bgp summary” on router1 and router2 reports State=Established, prefixes exchanged (each advertises its /24), and the routes are present in the kernel RIBs via eth0. Interfaces are up and healthy (ethtool shows Link detected: yes; tc and ip -s link show no errors/drops).

The only irregularity found was a single startup handshake hiccup: router1’s log shows “BGP OPEN receipt failed” followed by a Cease: connection collision, and neighbor stats show 1 Notification sent. This is a benign, one-time event that can occur when both peers initiate the TCP session simultaneously. After that, the session has remained established, with only routine keepalives every 60 seconds; there is no evidence of periodic resets.

Localization: router1<->router2 BGP over eth0. Affected component: initial BGP session establishment. Root cause: one-time connection collision during the first OPEN exchange; not persistent.

Corrective fix: No changes required. The network is operating normally. If users still observe intermittent “hang ups,” please provide timestamps so we can correlate with frr.log; if flaps recur, we can enable BFD or shorten BGP timers as a hardening measure, but current evidence does not indicate an ongoing fault.
